steps.body: To compare two-digit numbers, look at the tens first. 45 vs 52: 4 tens is less than 5 tens, so 45 < 52. More tens means a bigger number. The sign < points to the smaller one.
See which number sits farther right.

widget.prompt: The marker starts at 45. Drag it to 52.

commonPlacements.feedback: 48 still has 4 tens. Keep moving right until the tens digit becomes 5.
50 has the right number of tens but no ones yet. Move two more spots.

widget.successFeedback: 52 sits to the right of 45. Five tens is more than four tens.
widget.lowFeedback: The marker is still below 52. Move right.
widget.highFeedback: The marker has passed 52. Move left.

predict.prompt: 52 has one more ten than 45. Which way will the marker move?
predict.reveal: The marker moves right from 45 to 52. The tens decide first: 5 tens is more than 4 tens.

widget.gtFeedback: Check the tens first: 4 tens is less than 5 tens, so 45 < 52.
widget.eqFeedback: They aren't equal: 45 has 4 tens and 52 has 5 tens, so 45 < 52.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 4 tens is less than 5 tens, so 45 < 52.

explanationVariants: 6 tens is more than 3 tens, so 63 > 38.
63 has more tens than 38, so it's greater.

widget.successFeedback: Yes — 6 tens is more than 3 tens, so 63 > 38.
widget.ltFeedback: Check the tens: 6 tens is more than 3 tens, so 63 > 38.
widget.eqFeedback: They aren't equal: 63 has 6 tens and 38 has 3 tens, so 63 > 38.

steps.body: The number with more tens is greater, even if its ones are smaller. 40 has more tens than 39, so 40 > 39 — even though 0 ones is less than 9 ones.
Don't be fooled by the ones.

widget.ltFeedback: The 9 ones look big, but tens come first: 4 tens > 3 tens, so 40 > 39.
widget.eqFeedback: They aren't equal: 40 has 4 tens and 39 has 3 tens, so 40 > 39.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 4 tens is more than 3 tens, so 40 > 39.

steps.body: The symbol opens toward the bigger number: > means the left is greater, < means the left is smaller. 28 < 71 because 2 tens is less than 7 tens.

widget.gtFeedback: Check the tens: 2 tens is less than 7 tens, so 28 < 71.
widget.eqFeedback: They aren't equal: 28 has 2 tens and 71 has 7 tens, so 28 < 71.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 2 tens is less than 7 tens, so 28 < 71.

widget.eqFeedback: They aren't equal: 17 has 1 ten and 60 has 6 tens, so 17 < 60.

hints: Count the tens in each number.

steps.body: Compare the tens first — more tens means greater.
takeaways: Look at the tens digit first.
More tens wins, even with smaller ones.
The sign opens toward the bigger number.

concept.body: To compare two-digit numbers, look at the tens first. More tens means a bigger number. 45 vs 52: 4 tens < 5 tens, so 45 < 52 — even the ones don't matter yet.
